cohort: The study included 144 premature infants, divided into an experimental group (n=72) receiving low-dose glucocorticoids and a control group (n=72) receiving routine clinical care.
finding: Low-dose glucocorticoids significantly increased serum IL-10, decreased IL-8 and TGF-b1 levels, reduced the incidence (13.89%) and severity of bronchopulmonary dysplasia in preterm infants, and exhibited high safety.
